column1: # Canonical definition of the preconditions an integration run must satisfy
# before any suite is allowed to execute.
# Two classes, and the distinction is the whole point of this file:
#   SAFETY          failing means running anything further would be unsafe or
#                   semantically invalid -- a destructive suite could reach a
#                   database that is not disposable, or two worktrees could
#                   tear down each other's containers. The run aborts and NO
#                   suite is attempted. This is the fail-fast that must be
#                   preserved.
#   INFRASTRUCTURE  failing means no valid environment could be created, so
#                   the run cannot produce evidence about the system at all.
#                   Also aborts, but says something different: not "unsafe",
#                   rather "unable to observe".
# A functional test failure is neither of these. It is recorded and the run
# continues -- see scripts/integration-suites.tsv.
# Columns, tab separated:
#   id       stable identifier, appears in the evidence manifest
#   class    SAFETY | INFRASTRUCTURE
#   command  shell command; non-zero exit fails the precondition
# Order matters: checks that need a live database come after the one that
# starts it.
id
compose-isolation
destructive-authorization
postgres-healthy
disposable-database
schema-bootstrap
